source_notes.label: Temperature cycling and the comparison routes
source_notes.summary: The authors cool the reaction after injection to 80 °C and then reheat to 370 °C. They report teardrop CdSe cores and asymmetric head–tail CdSe/CdS rods. Separate constant-370 °C preparations are described as symmetric rods with single emission spectra, but their charges and dwell times are not separately specified.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sections 2.3 and 3; Figure 4

source_notes.label: The larger-seed TOP omission is a separate recipe option
source_notes.summary: The core method states that the separate 1.5 mL TOP addition is omitted for large-size seeds. This does not remove the 1.5 mL TOP used with selenium. No numerical dimension or displayed specimen is explicitly assigned to that variant, so the Figure 2(a) dimensions remain with the representative cycled-core route.

source_notes.label: Particle dimensions do not locate an internal interface
source_notes.summary: TEM gives core dimensions 10.5 ± 0.7 nm by 6.4 ± 0.4 nm, with aspect ratio 1.7 ± 0.1. For CdSe/CdS rods, the thicker head/stem is 18.3 ± 1.8 nm by 7.7 ± 0.8 nm, with aspect ratio 2.4 ± 0.3; the total length is 44.8 ± 4.1 nm. The authors propose that the head contains the CdSe core. The images do not supply a measured internal interface or shell-thickness map. Approximately 70% are classified as head–tail rods.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 2 and discussion

source_notes.label: Double emission is not proof of two size populations
source_notes.summary: The purified cores show approximate absorption features at 633 and 580 nm and PL peaks at 582 and 649 nm. No clear bimodal TEM size distribution is observed. After CdS growth the emission peaks shift to about 622 and 663 nm; relative quantum yield rises from about 3% to about 38%. The authors connect the optical behavior to varied faceting or morphology, without resolving separate particle populations.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 1 and discussion

source_notes.label: Wurtzite assignment and the growth model
source_notes.summary: Powder XRD assigns both cycled products to wurtzite. The source identifies reflections at 35° and 46° as characteristic CdSe <102> and <103>, and describes stronger relative <002> intensity for elongated particles. A shift from bulk CdSe toward CdS is interpreted as shell growth; no numerical refined lattice constant is supplied. The proposed mechanism invokes ligand-limited growth during cooling and renewed anisotropic growth on reheating.

source_notes.label: Two source schematic labels remain unresolved
source_notes.summary: Figure 4 labels growth <001>, whereas the prose discusses <002>. Its cycle label is 80–370–80 °C, whereas the method records the initial injection, cooling to 80 °C, reheating to 370 °C and room-temperature workup. These are retained as source differences; no silently corrected crystal direction or final 80 °C hold is imposed. The 10 min final anneal is explicit in the core discussion, not independently repeated in the shell procedure.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, Section 2.3, Section 3 and Figure 4
